world.rationale: Rapid capability gains (multi-hour METR task horizons in 2026) make superintelligence by 2050 close to a coin flip and likely by 2100, and loss of control or misuse then dominates doom risk. Without SI, doom stays a few percent, driven by nuclear war and engineered pandemics, and is slightly raised because some no-SI worlds are ones where a catastrophe halted progress; climate and resource stress are severe but rarely irreversible at civilizational scale. Global abundance demands 90% of a population increasingly concentrated in sub-Saharan Africa to have all five essentials including security and 75+ life expectancy, which trend growth alone rarely delivers but SI-driven abundance plausibly can.

countries.rationale: France already meets nearly every threshold (83-year life expectancy, universal electricity and water), so abundance is mainly a question of avoiding global catastrophe and a European war; food insecurity near 9% and aging are the main reasons abundance is not higher.

Great wealth and adaptive capacity, but higher fragility, food insecurity around 11%, status as a primary nuclear target and as the likely site of SI development raise collapse risk; unequal health and food access are the main barrier to the 90% abundance threshold.

Strong state capacity and high living standards favor abundance, but a Taiwan conflict with the US, political instability, northern water stress and an extreme 1.0 fertility rate straining care for the elderly are the main risks.

Extreme water stress, groundwater depletion, lethal heat and the risk of nuclear war with Pakistan drive collapse risk, while fast growth and near-universal electricity make reaching the 90% threshold plausible by 2100, especially with SI.

Very high fragility, ethnic grievance, insurgency and rapid population growth make a long civil war or state failure the dominant collapse route; starting from 55-year life expectancy, 30% safe water and 77% food insecurity, 90% abundance by 2100 is unlikely without SI.

Abundant water, hydro and renewables and food surpluses keep collapse risk low; high criminal violence, inequality and gaps in sanitation are the main obstacles to the 90% abundance threshold, with Amazon dieback a tail risk.

A densely populated low-lying delta faces sea-level rise, cyclones and salinization that threaten food and water, plus high fragility and grievance; strong recent gains in electricity and life expectancy give a real but uncertain path to abundance.

Near-total dependence on the Nile under extreme water stress, heavy food imports, a growing population and regime fragility make water and food the main collapse routes; cheap energy for desalination, especially with SI, is the main path to abundance.
